title: Refuse whole-disk searches before they stall the turn
when: A Bash command would search a whole-disk root with find, bfs, fd, rg, grep -r, du or tree, or would query locate or mdfind without -onlyin.
need: Roots resolving to /, /System, /Users, /Volumes, /private, /home or /mnt are refused by lint-broad-filesystem-scan, including relative roots after a cd, a glob whose static prefix is such a root, the working directory when no root is written, and commands nested in bash -c or zsh -c. The refusal names the tool and root, says the scan can block the turn so Yoke messages cannot arrive, and offers rg --files -g, find in the checkout, mdfind -onlyin, or asking the owning tool for a module path (python3 -c, pip show -f, npm root, brew --prefix). Home roots stay an advisory under lint-local-privacy; scoped roots such as the checkout or /tmp run normally.
surface: Client-local and core broad-scan refusals share one classifier and refusal text; the client denial row records the registered check id.
review: Source regression cases cover every refused and allowed shape on both hook paths with identical decisions and text, the implicit working-directory root, warn mode, and the client denial row carrying lint-broad-filesystem-scan with its session id. Live installed delivery on claude-cli and codex-cli is owed by the item's post-deploy QA.
